paper.one_line_finding: Within person, stories written with GPT-3.5 available scored higher on MAoSS originality (M = .56 vs .52; t(262) = 5.56, p < .001, d = .34; p. 14) and contributed less to semantic diversity (t(262) = -1.99, p = .047, d = -.123; p. 17) than the same 263 analyzed students' stories written without AI (Figure 2, p. 15).

Its Study 1 reanalyzes this paper's 263 analyzed participants and cites this paper as Luchini et al. (2025c), so the two papers share one sample. The c159 PDF (v3, posted 2025-05-26) names no other paper using these participants.

studies.label: Within-subjects story writing with and without ChatGPT (GPT-3.5), randomized order

counts_source.quote: In total, our final sample consisted of 263 participants

arms.name: AI-help
arms.description: Each participant wrote one story with ChatGPT available in a side textbox. A hidden system prompt constrained responses to bullet-point ideas and prevented entire story passages; copying and pasting was disabled. Before either scored condition, participants completed a practice story with ChatGPT available. PDF pp. 9-10, Story Writing Task; Appendix A, PDF p. 32.

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: The same participants wrote one story in the matched interface with the ChatGPT textbox removed. Participants were instructed to use the suggested prompting strategies as self-directed brainstorming. All completed a practice story with ChatGPT available before either scored condition; the paper does not establish that every person actually used ChatGPT during practice. PDF pp. 9-11, Story Writing Task; Appendix B, PDF p. 32.

studies.task: Write a creative story of at least 150 words using all words in either pen-paper-write or year-week-embark, with prompts counterbalanced across conditions (PDF pp. 9-10).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT based on the GPT 3.5 base model, accessed through a custom API
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Method, Story Writing Task: "A custom API was used to call ChatGPT based on the GPT 3.5 base model." No model release year or exact API snapshot is stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is stated in the full document or Appendices A-D. PDF p. 8 names originality and diversity as the main outcomes and provides an OSF data link; a data link is not evidence of preregistration.

studies.shared_sample: Study 1 of c475, Luchini, Kaufman, and Beaty, Generative AI Does Not Erase Individual Differences in Human Creativity, reanalyzes this sample according to forms/c159.json, sample_overlap. This relationship is carried from the reconciled form as instructed; the c159 PDF does not name the later paper.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Multilingual Assessment of Short Stories (MAoSS), a fine-tuned language model trained to predict human-rated story originality, available on the Creativity Assessment Platform (PDF p. 11, Scoring, Originality). The paper states a 0 to 1 scale (PDF p. 18, Self-Assessment Accuracy). One scored story per participant per condition.

stats.difference_is: AI-help minus No-AI; no numeric mean difference is printed.

paper_effect.standardizer: Not stated; the result accompanies a paired-samples t-test, but the paper does not identify the SD used.

estimates.notes: The PDF prints both arm SDs as "SD = 08", with no decimal point. The numeric SD fields are null because the intended value cannot be confirmed without correcting the paper; the exact printing is retained in the source quote. The reported 95% CI [.021, .045] follows t, p, and d without identifying its target; its bounds are transcribed in stats.ci_lower and stats.ci_upper, with ci_of null. It is not assigned to d. No mean difference, SE, SD of paired differences, or within-person outcome correlation is printed. No quantities were calculated. The unit and SD level are participant because each person contributes one story in each condition. The reported paired t-test treats people as the analysis units. PDF p. 8 identifies originality and diversity as the two main outcomes; no preregistration is stated. Figure 2 on PDF p. 15 shows confidence-interval error bars without numeric endpoints; no numbers were read from the plot. Only the full-sample paired contrast is reported; no first-round or order-specific contrast is available.

estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Leave-one-out contribution of each story to its prompt-specific dataset: the dataset mean of all pairwise semantic distances (1 minus cosine similarity), minus the same mean with that story removed. Uses final-layer sentence embeddings from paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2; prompt words are removed before embedding. Datasets are split by writing prompt rather than condition. Positive scores mean the story adds diversity. Methods: PDF pp. 11-12; Figure 1, PDF p. 13. One contribution score per participant per condition.

stats.difference_is: AI-help minus No-AI; no numeric mean difference is printed.

paper_effect.standardizer: Not stated; the result accompanies a paired-samples t-test, but the paper does not identify the SD used.

estimates.notes: Means, SDs, and the reported CI are retained in the units printed in the Results. Figure 2 (PDF p. 15) multiplies diversity contribution by 10^3 only for plotting; no conversion was applied and no numeric CI endpoints were read from that figure. The reported 95% CI [-0.0001, -0.0000006] follows t, p, and d without identifying its target; ci_of is null and these bounds are not assigned to d. Both arm levels are mean per-story contributions to prompt-specific reference pools. Because prompts were counterbalanced across conditions (PDF p. 9) and the diversity datasets were split by prompt only (PDF pp. 11-12), the reference pools mix conditions; this is an inference from the stated method. The paper does not report separate within-arm set diversity. Higher scores mean more diverse output. The negative reported contrast indicates lower diversity contributions with AI. The reported uncertainty is a paired t-test across participants, not a test treating all story pairs as independent. Each participant contributes one score per condition, although scores share reference pools; no adjustment for that shared-pool dependence is described. No numeric mean difference, SE, paired-difference SD, or within-person outcome correlation is printed. PDF p. 8 identifies this as a main outcome. Only the full-sample paired contrast is available; no first-round or order-specific contrast is reported.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: Self-assessed story originality and self-assessment accuracy, including self-rating correlations with MAoSS, the condition-by-self-assessment interaction, and self-assessment error
not_extracted.reason: Self-reports and calibration of self-reports are excluded, even when compared with an objective score; these are not qualifying creativity or diversity outcomes (PDF p. 11, Scoring, Self-Assessment; PDF pp. 17-18, Self-Assessment Accuracy).

not_extracted.reason: Correlational process/moderation analyses rather than contrasts between randomly assigned assistance conditions; integration and prompting behavior were not randomized (PDF pp. 14-16, Story Originality; Appendix D, PDF p. 34).

not_extracted.reason: Correlational process/moderation analyses rather than contrasts between randomly assigned assistance conditions; integration and prompting behavior were not randomized (PDF p. 17, Story Diversity; Appendix D, PDF p. 34).

not_extracted.reason: Association between AI interaction behaviors within the AI-help condition, not an outcome contrast on participants' creative output (PDF p. 16, Story Originality).

not_extracted.what: Interrater reliability of the prompt classification scheme
not_extracted.reason: Reliability of process coding, not a creativity outcome scored on the produced stories or an assigned-arm contrast (PDF p. 14, Prompt Classification).

not_extracted.reason: Used only to adjust correlations; no full-sample AI-help versus No-AI contrast statistics are printed for word count (PDF pp. 15-17).

not_extracted.what: Other classical creativity tasks, cognitive tasks, and questionnaires in the session
not_extracted.reason: The paper describes these as outside its research questions and prints no eligible randomized assistance contrast for their outcomes (PDF p. 9, Procedure).

not_extracted.what: AI-response integration score itself (similarity between an AI-help story and that participant’s AI responses)
not_extracted.reason: A process measure used in observational correlations with originality and diversity gains; no full-sample randomized AI-help versus No-AI or AI-configuration contrast is reported. Similarity to AI responses is distinct from diversity across different people. PDF p. 12, Integration of AI Responses; PDF pp. 14-17, Results.

open_items: Originality arm SDs require confirmation: the PDF literally prints "08" for both, so both numeric SD fields are null (PDF p. 14). No SD was computed from participant data.

For both eligible contrasts, the paper does not identify the estimand of its printed confidence interval or the standardizer used for d. ci_of is null; no paired-difference SD, within-person correlation, or SE is printed (PDF pp. 14 and 17).
The paper reports recruitment, not a count explicitly randomized to each condition order. Counts at assignment, analyzed counts by order, and exclusions by order remain unavailable (PDF pp. 8-9).

No first-round-only results or order/carryover analysis are reported. All participants had a practice story with ChatGPT available before both main conditions; actual practice use by every person is unstated (PDF pp. 9-11).
The diversity outcome uses prompt-specific pools that mix conditions; within-arm set diversity is not reported (PDF pp. 11-12).
The paper does not state a release year or exact API snapshot for its GPT 3.5 base model; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 10).
